$comment: Everyday phrases that explain a symptom without a medication being involved — "after yard work", "from the heat". detective.ts uses them to avoid implying a link that the person logging the symptom has already explained. NOT clinical content, and no citation needed: these are plain English, not medical claims. HISTORY (2026-10-01): this file used to carry common/urgent side-effect lists for 79 medications, plus 53 name synonyms. Both were removed, and the reason is the point. The G1-23 reframing on 2026-09-13 deliberately stopped the app judging symptoms — "no side-effect matching, no urgency, no reassurance" — which left that data unread by any code while still shipping inside the app binary: unreviewed clinical content with nothing surfacing it. It was written by an AI in a single commit and had never had a clinician look at it, so it could not have been revived as-is anyway. Deleted on Hana's decision rather than kept "for later". It is in git history (see 63444cd for the cited version) if the feature is ever genuinely rebuilt — in which case the symptom lists need a clinical review first, not a re-import. verify-med-knowledge.js now fails if per-medication clinical content reappears here, so the G1-23 decision is enforced by a check rather than by memory.
